findings.issue_text: Crash on empty/missing destinationCalendar in Google Meet fallback: destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty — the exact case this branch exists to handle

Tautological calendar-id fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent (CalendarService.ts:256-258 and 315-317): when externalCalendarId is falsy, `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match, so the fallback always returns undefined and events.update/delete is called with calendarId: undefined, failing to update/delete the correct calendar event

Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService always use destinationCalendar[0] instead of matching credentialId, so for collective events a member's credential authenticates as member B but posts to the main host's calendar ID, causing 404/failure and no event in member B's calendar

Inverted slug logic in organization creation (create.handler.ts:151-152): with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED disabled the org now gets neither slug nor requestedSlug (previously it got slug), losing the slug and making the org unreachable via slug; with billing enabled it now sets both — behavior change unrelated to the PR's purpose

Booking references regress to externalCalendarId: undefined when destination calendar has no credentialId: createEvent(c, event) is called without the externalId parameter, so EventManager stores undefined externalCalendarId on the booking reference, feeding the dead lookup in update/delete

Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none (handleNewBooking.ts:1080-1082): if evt.destinationCalendar is null, the optional-chained push is a no-op, so all teamDestinationCalendars are discarded and collective events create no calendar events without error

user.destinationCalendar may not be loaded where consumed (handleNewBooking.ts:995-1000): the dynamic-link query select and eventType hosts/users shapes were not changed to include destinationCalendar, so it may always be undefined, silently disabling the feature for dynamic collective links and eventType.users fallback

Duplicate recurring-event deletion passes per calendar reference (handleCancelBooking.ts:415-479): with N collective calendar references, every calendar event deletion is attempted N×N times, producing noisy 404/410 errors and redundant API load on recurring collective cancellations

Silent fallback to 'primary' calendar (CalendarService.ts:157-159): if no destination matches credentialId, the event is created in 'primary' with no warning, so users who selected a specific calendar silently get events on their primary calendar

Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback in CalendarService.ts (lines 253-256 and 312-315) compares destinationCalendar entries against undefined externalCalendarId, so legacy bookings without externalCalendarId on the reference silently no-op on calendar event update/delete

Same N+1 credential fetch pattern in updateAllCalendarEvents: prisma.credential.findUnique awaited per calendar reference inside the loop, serializing DB fetches and updateEvent calls; should be replaced with one batched lookup keyed by collected reference.credentialIds

Recurring-booking deletion block nested inside the per-reference loop in handleCancelBooking.ts causes O(R × C × B) deleteEvent external API calls, multiplying calls (e.g., ~20 to ~100 for 5 hosts, 10 bookings, 2 credentials) with repeated deletion attempts against already-deleted events
N+1 credential fetch in cancel handler: awaited prisma.credential.findUnique per reference inside the bookingCalendarReference loop; batchable with findMany before the loop

Fallback fan-out in createAllCalendarEvents: for destinations without credentialId, createEvent is called via every matching credential per destination, multiplying external API calls and duplicate event creation attempts for multiple legacy destinations of the same type

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tautological calendar-id fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent (CalendarService.ts:256-258 and 315-317): when externalCalendarId is falsy, `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match, so the fallback always returns undefined and events.update/delete is called with calendarId: undefined, failing to update/delete the correct calendar event

Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService always use destinationCalendar[0] instead of matching credentialId, so for collective events a member's credential authenticates as member B but posts to the main host's calendar ID, causing 404/failure and no event in member B's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `destinationCalendar` was changed from a single object to an array (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination/credential pairing. However, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (and its related methods) and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` ignore which destination is being targeted and instead do `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then use only `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` to pick the calendar ID/URL. That means when iterating for a non-first destination (e.g., member B), the service can authenticate with member B’s credential but still attempt to write to destinationCalendar[0] (likely the main host’s calendar ID), which is a concrete mismatch introduced by this diff and can plausibly cause API failure/404 and missing events for the other member calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking references regress to externalCalendarId: undefined when destination calendar has no credentialId: createEvent(c, event) is called without the externalId parameter, so EventManager stores undefined externalCalendarId on the booking reference, feeding the dead lookup in update/delete

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating destinations, the `else` branch for a destination without `credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no third argument). But `createEvent` was changed to accept an optional `externalId` and now returns it as `result.externalId`, and later code stores booking reference `externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId` (see changes around `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined`). Therefore for destinations without `credentialId`, the created event result will carry `externalId: undefined`, causing booking references to lose `externalCalendarId`, which can break later update/delete logic that relies on that value.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references logic in `handleNewBooking.ts` (lines 1080-1082) about an optional-chained `push` on `evt.destinationCalendar` being a no-op when null. That file and code path are not present anywhere in the provided diff, so the claim cannot be verified against these changes. The diff shown mainly changes `destinationCalendar` to be an array in several places (e.g., `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `EventManager.ts`, calendar services), but does not include the alleged `handleNewBooking.ts` behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `handleNewBooking.ts:995-1000` and claims related Prisma `select`/shape changes were not made to include `destinationCalendar`. None of that code (handleNewBooking.ts, its queries, or the dynamic-link query) appears in the provided diff, so this cannot be verified as a problem introduced or present in the diff. The diff only shows changes in other files (e.g., bookingReminder, CalendarManager/EventManager, handleCancelBooking) adapting `destinationCalendar` to an array, but does not show any missing `destinationCalendar` selection/loading in handleNewBooking or dynamic-link logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate recurring-event deletion passes per calendar reference (handleCancelBooking.ts:415-479): with N collective calendar references, every calendar event deletion is attempted N×N times, producing noisy 404/410 errors and redundant API load on recurring collective cancellations

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In handleCancelBooking.ts the code changed from `.find(...)` (single calendar reference) to `.filter(...)` (array) and then iterates `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that loop, for the recurring-event branch it builds `promises` over *all* `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(type.endsWith('_calendar'))` and for each credential iterates `updatedBookings` and deletes based on `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes('_calendar'))`. That inner deletion logic does not use the outer `reference` values (uid/externalCalendarId) and will therefore be executed redundantly once per calendar reference in `bookingCalendarReference`, causing repeated delete attempts of the same events and extra API calls (and likely extra 404/410s). The exact multiplier is at least linear in the number of references (outer loop), not necessarily strictly N×N, but the duplication problem is real and introduced by this diff.

Unguarded access to mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration in EventManager.ts:114-117 throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty and location is Google Meet, crashing booking creation instead of falling back to Cal Video

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts the diff introduces `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` inside `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError if `evt.location` is `MeetLocationType` (because the RHS of `&&` is then evaluated). The diff also changes `destinationCalendar` to be an array and sometimes sets it to `[]`, making this scenario plausible.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding refers to a logic inversion in `organizations/create.handler.ts` around lines 148-154, but that file (and any `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`/slug logic) does not appear anywhere in the provided diff. The diff only touches booking reminders, calendar services, CalendarManager/EventManager, calendar event types, and cancellation handling. Therefore the issue described cannot be verified as being introduced or present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credentials fetched from DB by raw ID with no ownership/tenant check in EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents (~line 345), updateAllEvents (~line 510), and handleCancelBooking.ts (~line 425), removing the prior ownership boundary and enabling potential cross-tenant calendar write/delete (IDOR-shaped)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds fallback logic that, when a credentialId is present but not found in the in-memory scoped credential lists, fetches a credential by `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: ... } })` and then uses it to create/update/delete calendar events. This occurs in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (new DB fetch for `destination.credentialId`), EventManager.updateAllEvents (new DB fetch for `reference.credentialId`), and handleCancelBooking (new DB fetch for `credentialId`). In all cases, the query is by raw ID only and the returned credential is used without checking that it belongs to the current user/team/tenant (e.g., matching `userId`/`teamId`). Previously these paths were bounded by `this.calendarCredentials` / `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`; the new DB fallback removes that boundary and is an IDOR-shaped cross-tenant write/delete risk if an attacker can influence/forge a `credentialId` in destinationCalendar/references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback in CalendarService.ts (lines 253-256 and 312-315) compares destinationCalendar entries against undefined externalCalendarId, so legacy bookings without externalCalendarId on the reference silently no-op on calendar event update/delete

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the GoogleCalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent changes, the fallback path when externalCalendarId is falsy uses `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. If `externalCalendarId` is undefined/null (e.g., legacy references missing it), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will not match any real calendar, so the result is `undefined`. The code then falls back to `"primary"` (update uses defaultCalendarId; delete similarly), meaning it will attempt to update/delete the event in the wrong calendar and likely fail (e.g., 404), effectively preventing updates/deletes for those bookings. This is directly verifiable in the diff at the noted lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Collective members' calendar IDs (externalId/email addresses) are newly exposed in webhook payloads via evt.destinationCalendar in handleNewBooking.ts:1084, disclosing team member calendar identifiers to third-party webhook consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any changes to `handleNewBooking.ts` (or any webhook payload construction) at the cited location, so the claim about “newly exposed in webhook payloads” is not verifiable from this patch. adjudication_records.issue_text: Google createEvent in CalendarService.ts:145-148 silently falls back to the credential's 'primary' calendar when no destinationCalendar entry matches the credentialId, violating explicit destination-calendar selection

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` only by finding a `destinationCalendar` entry whose `credentialId === credentialId` (new parameter), and then calls `calendar.events.insert` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If the event has destination calendars but none match the credential being used (e.g., entries have no `credentialId`, mismatched IDs, or the code is creating events for multiple credentials), the code will silently fall back to inserting into the Google account’s `primary` calendar, ignoring the explicitly provided destination-calendar selection. This behavior is directly present in the diff and can result in events being created on the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Collective destination calendars are silently dropped in handleNewBooking.ts:1084 when evt.destinationCalendar is null (optional chain short-circuits), so events are created in none of the members' intended destinations

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `handleNewBooking.ts:1084`, but that file/line is not part of the provided diff, so the claimed behavior (optional chaining short-circuit dropping collective destination calendars there) is not verifiable from this change set. The diff shown primarily changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and updates other code paths (e.g., `EventManager`, `handleCancelBooking`, calendar services) to handle arrays, but it does not demonstrate the specific bug described in `handleNewBooking.ts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sequential await of createEvent for each destination calendar in createAllCalendarEvents causes booking latency to grow linearly with number of collective hosts; independent calls could run concurrently

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and does `await createEvent(...)` inside the loop when `destination.credentialId` is set. That makes calendar event creations run sequentially per destination, so total booking time will grow roughly linearly with the number of destination calendars. These calls appear independent (each destination calendar insertion), and only the non-credentialId branch uses `Promise.all`, so the sequential behavior is verifiable in the diff and is a performance regression introduced by supporting multiple destinations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 credential fetches: prisma.credential.findUnique is awaited per destination inside the createAllCalendarEvents loop instead of one batched findMany by IDs

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and, when a matching credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } ... })` inside that loop. That means multiple destinations with missing cached credentials will trigger multiple sequential DB queries (an N+1 pattern) rather than a single batched `findMany` by all needed IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same N+1 credential fetch pattern in updateAllCalendarEvents: prisma.credential.findUnique awaited per calendar reference inside the loop, serializing DB fetches and updateEvent calls; should be replaced with one batched lookup keyed by collected reference.credentialIds

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` within `updateAllCalendarEvents`, the diff introduces a `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop where, if a matching credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })` inside the loop. Because this `await` is inside the loop, multiple references will trigger multiple sequential DB round-trips (an N+1 pattern) and also serialize the `updateEvent(...)` scheduling per reference (they are pushed one-by-one after awaited work). This is a verifiable performance/scalability issue present in the diff and could be improved by batching credential lookups by collected `credentialId`s before the loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recurring-booking deletion block nested inside the per-reference loop in handleCancelBooking.ts causes O(R × C × B) deleteEvent external API calls, multiplying calls (e.g., ~20 to ~100 for 5 hosts, 10 bookings, 2 credentials) with repeated deletion attempts against already-deleted events

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, bookingCalendarReference was changed from a single reference via .find(...) to an array via .filter(...), and the deletion logic is now wrapped in `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. The recurring-booking deletion branch (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) performs deletes by iterating over *all* calendar credentials and *all* updatedBookings and calling `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` for each booking ref found. Because this whole recurring deletion block is now inside the per-reference loop, it will run once per calendar reference (R), multiplying external delete calls by R and likely re-attempting deletion of the same events multiple times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 credential fetch in cancel handler: awaited prisma.credential.findUnique per reference inside the bookingCalendarReference loop; batchable with findMany before the loop

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the diff changes bookingCalendarReference from a single .find(...) result to an array via .filter(...). The new code then loops `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` and, when a matching credential is not found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` inside that loop. This creates one DB query per reference in the worst case (N+1 pattern) and is directly verifiable from the shown diff; it could be batched with a single `findMany` on all missing credentialIds before iterating.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent: `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against undefined in the else-branch, so fallback never matches and `calendarId: undefined` is sent to the Google API, causing 400/404 failures on reschedule/delete for bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255-257, 314-317)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the new fallback branch is logically broken:

- updateEvent: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`
- deleteEvent: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`

In both cases the `:` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (typically `undefined`/`null`). But it then tries to find a destination calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` — i.e., equals `undefined`/`null` — which will not match normal calendars, so it returns `undefined`.

This is a regression from the prior behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) which would have selected the event’s destination calendar id when no `externalCalendarId` was provided. With the new code, the calendar id becomes `undefined` (or forces whatever later fallback is used, e.g. primary), which can lead to failures when updating/deleting events that were created in a non-primary calendar and the reference doesn’t carry `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking references lose externalCalendarId in the no-credentialId destination path: createEvent is called without the new externalId argument, so result.externalId is undefined and stored as externalCalendarId on the reference, regressing stored data and feeding the broken Google fallback (packages/core/EventManager.ts:374-379, 169)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the new `createEvent` signature is `createEvent(credential, calEvent, externalId?)` and `CalendarManager.createEvent` now returns `{ externalId, credentialId: credential.id }`, with `externalId` coming only from that optional argument. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch where a destination calendar has no `credentialId` calls `await createEvent(c, event)` (no third argument) when iterating `destinationCalendarCredentials`. That makes `result.externalId` undefined for those created events. Later, when building booking/reference data, the diff shows `externalCalendarId` is now taken from `result.externalId` (e.g. `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined`), so this path will store `externalCalendarId` as undefined even if the destination calendar had an `externalId` available. This is a concrete regression introduced by the diff (missing argument) and can break later update/delete logic that relies on `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reschedule merge cleanup in EventManager.ts ~551-556 uses .find() and deletes only the first _calendar reference, orphaning old calendar events in other collective members' calendars

However, in the reschedule/merge cleanup block (`if (newBookingId) { ... }`) it still does `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which selects only the first matching calendar reference. If there are multiple `_calendar` references (e.g., collective/multi-destination calendars), only one old calendar event will be deleted and the others can remain orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pre-existing async executor in new Promise in googlecalendar CalendarService.ts (createEvent ~100-107, updateEvent ~196-198): a rejection inside the async executor leaves the outer promise forever pending with no timeout, hanging the booking flow

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `createEvent` and `updateEvent` wrap logic in `return new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => { ... })`. Because the Promise constructor does not observe/chain the promise returned by an `async` executor, any thrown error or rejected `await` inside that executor (e.g., `await this.auth.getToken()`, Google API calls, etc.) will not call `reject` and can leave the *outer* promise pending indefinitely (often surfacing as an unhandled rejection). This behavior is a real correctness defect present in the diff (the pattern remains in the modified functions).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/broken lookup in Google CalendarService.updateEvent (lines 255-257) — `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` with falsy externalCalendarId can never match, so legacy bookings without externalCalendarId fail to update on the calendar

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent`, the new selection logic is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null), the fallback branch runs but then searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value, which will almost never match. Previously, the code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (when it was a single object), so updates could still target the intended calendar without an `externalCalendarId` reference.

With this diff, updates for events that rely on `event.destinationCalendar` (and don’t have `externalCalendarId` stored in the reference) will resolve `selectedCalendar` to `undefined` and likely update the wrong calendar (e.g., default/primary) or fail to find the event on that calendar. This is a concrete, verifiable logic defect introduced by the change to an array-based `destinationCalendar`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same dead lookup in Google CalendarService.deleteEvent (lines 313-316) — the find with falsy externalCalendarId is a no-op, resulting in an API error or deletion targeted at the wrong calendar ('primary'), leaving a stale event in the real destination

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent`, the new logic sets `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the case this fallback is meant to handle), the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will almost always return no match, yielding `undefined`. Given the nearby `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, the delete call will then likely fall back to deleting from `primary` (or pass an undefined calendarId), instead of the actual destination calendar, risking a failed deletion or deletion in the wrong calendar and leaving the real event stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guaranteed TypeError in EventManager.ts:117-118 — destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined, and accessing `.integration` on undefined throws when destinationCalendar is null, crashing the Google Meet without Google Calendar fallback path it's meant to handle

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts the new code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately checks `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined` and accessing `.integration` will throw a TypeError. This is a regression from the prior safe optional-chaining check `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== ...`, and it affects the Google Meet fallback path when no destination calendar is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Vacuous find() in Google CalendarService.ts updateEvent (253-256) and deleteEvent (312-315) — `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never be true in the fallback branch since externalCalendarId is falsy, passing calendarId: undefined to Google API and causing reschedules/cancellations to fail with orphaned calendar events

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, the fallback branch for selectedCalendar is:

`externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the condition that puts you in the fallback branch), the predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined` (or null), which will not match any normal destination calendar with a real externalId. So the fallback almost always returns `undefined`, unlike the previous logic which used the event’s destination calendar externalId. The same pattern exists in deleteEvent for `calendarId`.

As a result, update/delete calls can end up not using the intended destination calendar (potentially falling back to primary if later code defaults, or passing undefined if it doesn’t), causing the wrong calendar to be targeted and leaving orphaned events. This is a concrete correctness regression introduced by the diff (the find() is vacuous in the fallback path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: BaseCalendarService.createEvent (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:153-160) always selects destinationCalendar[0] regardless of executing credential — collective events with N members cause N duplicate events in the first member's calendar while other members' calendars receive nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` at `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:153-160`, so the claim is not verifiable against the provided changes. In the shown `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the calendar ID used for insertion is selected via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which explicitly does *not* always pick `destinationCalendar[0]`. The only place `destinationCalendar[0]` is used is for the organizer attendee email fallback (`mainHostDestinationCalendar`), not for selecting which calendar to insert into. Therefore the proposed finding misreads the diff / references code not present here.

matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

The candidate flags that updateAllCalendarEvents can call updateEvent with an undefined credential when the credential lookup fails (in memory and DB), matching the golden issue about credential being undefined when passed to updateEvent and causing runtime errors/crashes.
